A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same GMS-EB/GMS-DH research despite the changed title. Their main texts, figures, tables, equations and complete appendices are readable and support comparison across relocation and renumbering.

before.justification: Section 5 and Appendices B and E report original solver benchmarks, training curves, pruning ablations and zero-shot generalization results.

after.justification: Section 5 and Appendices C, F and G retain original empirical results and report additional pruning comparisons and multigraph evaluations.

M1.justification: The proposed GREAT encoders, preference-conditioned decoders, learned edge selection, REINFORCE objectives and curriculum remain unchanged. Additional probability equations explain the existing procedures. GMS-DH PP is introduced as a comparator, while GMS-DH Simple already appeared as an ablation in v1.

E1.justification: Appendix G extends the retained synthetic routing domain with FLEX5/FIX5 and FLEX10/FIX10 MGMOTSP scenarios and FIX2 MGMOTSPTW evaluation. These broaden parallel-edge and distribution coverage without introducing a new routing task. The original FLEX2-20 time-window results remain in Table 10.

E2.justification: v3 adds GMS-DH PP, which prunes before encoding, to the MGMOTSP comparison. It also adds the existing GMS-DH Simple variant to MGMOTSPTW comparisons in Tables 3 and 10-11. The external baseline families in corresponding original experiments are retained.

E3.justification: Table 13 introduces a zero-shot protocol holding node count at 100 while applying models trained on FLEX5/FIX5 to FLEX10/FIX10. Existing HV metrics, reference points and node-count generalization protocols are retained. Newly disclosed batch-size and ablation-budget details do not establish that earlier experiments changed.

E4.justification: v1's pruning ablation covered FLEX2-50 MGMOTSP. v3 extends it to FIX2, adds pre-encoding versus intermediate pruning comparisons, and directly ablates learned selection on MGMOTSPTW. Table 13 also tests unseen edge multiplicity. These substantially broaden the investigation of the central design's necessity and generalization.

E5.justification: Both versions report averages across instances without independent experimental run counts, seeds, confidence intervals or significance tests. The retained training curves and additional tables introduce no error bars or uncertainty-estimation procedures.

E6.justification: v3 adds substantive results for pruning controls, denser multigraphs and FIX2 time windows. Existing MOEA entries also change: Table 1's FLEX2-100 MOEA/D entry changes from HV 0.66, gap 30.28% and 12h to 0.68, 28.46% and 99h. The cause of these revisions is unexplained. Most original GMS benchmark values remain unchanged.

T1.justification: Section 4.1 refines decoder complexity from N^4 to O(MN^4), explicitly accounting for parallel-edge multiplicity M. Equation 19 also corrects the differentiated parameter in v1's selection-head gradient. Proposition 1 formalizes the existing linear-scalarization pruning observation; no proof is added.

C1.justification: The main claims remain first neural solvers for multigraph routing, applicability to asymmetric multi-objective problems, and competitive performance with an accuracy-versus-speed tradeoff between the two architectures. The rewritten abstract, introduction and conclusion preserve these contributions; additional experiments strengthen their support.

C2.justification: v3 hypothesizes that pre-pruning shifts the input distribution and reduces Pareto-front diversity, and explains MBM's speed and performance variation. Appendix F gives a more qualified pruning interpretation: simple pruning can be appropriate for MGMOTSP, whereas the time-window comparisons demonstrate greater benefits from learned selection.

D1.justification: v3 newly specifies batch size B = 64 and fourfold POMO sampling for the simple-pruning ablation to match the learned-pruning budget. Table 13 identifies the training regimes of transferred models. These improve reproducibility disclosures; both versions still promise code release upon acceptance.

R1.justification: v3 adds improvement-based routing literature, including Chen and Tian, Hottung and Tierney, and Hudson et al., alongside practical road-network motivation. Appendix A explicitly positions the mixed autoregressive/non-autoregressive construction. Much of that appendix relocates existing related work; the updated GREAT citation identifies the same work.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion are substantially rewritten, and the method explanation is expanded. Detailed related work moves into a new Appendix A, the pruning ablation moves into Appendix F, and experimental subsections are reordered. These substantially revise the narrative and organization beyond the added experiments.

P2.justification: Figures 1-3 receive notation and arrangement refinements. Tables gain comparator rows, distribution panels and second-best underlining, with additional time-window and edge-transfer displays. The ablation table is relocated and expanded. The original training plots and overall two-column visual format remain.

improvement.justification: v3 strengthens the pruning justification through direct learned-versus-simple comparisons on time-window tasks and a pre-encoding pruning control, addressing questions left open by v1's narrower ablation. Five-to-ten-edge transfer tests and more qualified interpretation further improve empirical support. These are focused gains within an otherwise stable paper; the unexplained MOEA score and runtime revisions remain a reporting limitation.
